Why the Quran is from God

A man named while he lived

A short sura names a living opponent, and scholars read it as saying he would not believe.

Most prophecy names nobody. One short sura names Abu Lahab, the Prophet's uncle and opponent, while he lived, and speaks of his end. Scholars read this as saying he would die without believing. He lived on for years. A word of belief, even a pretended one, would have given the Prophet's opponents their case against the sura. It never came, though it lay in one man's power to say it.

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ تَبَّتْ يَدَآ أَبِى لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ١ مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَمَا كَسَبَ٢ سَيَصْلَىٰ نَارًا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ٣﴾

Translation of the meaning

May the hands of Abū Lahab be ruined, and ruined is he. His wealth will not avail him or that which he gained. He will [enter to] burn in a Fire of [blazing] flame

Quran · Al-Masad 111:1-3

You might ask

QuestionIsn't the opening a curse, not a forecast?
AnswerIt can be read that way, and on that reading the sign is weaker. Scholars look instead to the later line about his end, which is in the future tense.Quran · Al-Masad 111:3
QuestionWasn't he a safe bet never to change?
AnswerSome would say so, since his hostility was open. Yet other fierce opponents did change, so the test lay in one man's hands for years, and he never said the word.Quran · Al-Masad 111:1
QuestionIs this a verdict on anyone alive today?
AnswerNo. It concerns one man in one life. The same book tells every reader, whatever they have done, not to despair of God's mercy.Quran · Az-Zumar 39:53

The sura handed one man the means to disprove it. He never used them.
